title: £80m dementia challenge to test AI and digital tools
source_used: News-Medical carrying the UKRI release (Digital Health page blocked)
key_facts: Nine technologies, including faster MRI brain scans and a remote cognitive assessment, will be tested in the NHS to speed dementia diagnosis, backed by up to £80 million.
Goal: 92% of people diagnosed within 18 weeks of referral, up from around 60% today, with diagnosis often taking more than a year.
Funded by the UK government through UK Research and Innovation's R&D Missions Accelerator Programme; projects get further funding only if they prove they work.
AI-linked projects: Minder, a home-monitoring platform with sensors and AI, and a University of Cambridge AI decision-support tool that predicts dementia progression from routine records.

Other projects: faster MRI (about 7 minutes instead of 20), blood biomarkers, the 15-minute Cognitron remote cognitive test, sleep apnoea screening, a sound-processing test and Scotland's service redesign.
Alzheimer's Society called it potentially a 'game changer' and urged a national 18-week target.
quote_evidence: Nine new technologies, including faster MRI brain scans and a remote cognitive assessment, will be tested in the NHS as part of a government drive to diagnose dementia faster.
Backed by up to £80 million, the goal is for 92% of people to be diagnosed within 18 weeks of a referral, up from around 60% today with diagnosis often taking more than a year.
why_it_matters_hint: Real-world NHS testing of tools to cut dementia diagnosis waits.
